newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up sharply in active trading on Friday, due to speculation triggered by overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,370 yuan ($2,334) per tonne, rising 260 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 19,500 and hit a low of 19,350.
November rose 60 to 18,950, December 110 to 19,160, January 290 to 19,400, March 240 to 19,360, April 250 to 19,380 and May 330 to 19,400.
Combined volume rose sharply to 87,200 tonnes from 21,880.
Copper opened higher and profit-taking and fresh selling pushed prices down but still up from Thursday's close.
"Stop loss buying emerged in the morning session, but copper met strong resistance at the 19,500-yuan level due to mixed opinions about the trend," one trader said.
"Much of the buying and selling was speculative today and copper is likely to fall next Monday if there is no further positive news," he added.
Traders said an expectation of LME stockpiles falling sharply on Friday triggered speculative buying today.
"Potential for further rises is limited due to lower spot copper prices if the expectation is confirmed, otherwise copper will fall sharply next Monday," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended up. November rose 120 to 13,480 yuan per tonne, December 100 to 13,320 and January 100 to 13,350.
Combined volume rose to 700 tonnes from 250.
